summary: IDENTITY PASS (lane I, no anchors). THE SOURCE: the catalog has source_kind=manga with NO manga link, and the reason is structural, not a data gap — AniList types the edge from anime 21175 to manga 86508 (Toyotaro/Toriyama, 'Dragon Ball Super', V-Jump, from 2015-06-20, 24 vols / 104 chapters) as ALTERNATIVE, not ADAPTATION, so pickManga correctly found no ADAPTATION edge (open flag #1016). AniList is right about the world: Kanzenshuu's Manga Guide states it outright — 'While both the manga and TV series are based on the same general story developed by Toriyama, each often go with their own separate take on events; this is in contrast to the development of the original Dragon Ball and Dragon Ball Z TV series, which were nearly direct adaptations of the original Dragon Ball manga series.' ja-WP says the same mechanically: Toriyama's outline is delivered as TEXT and 'the TV series' staff and the manga's staff each produce their work SIMULTANEOUSLY (同時進行) from that outline', and Toyotaro says it in the official vol-1 Tori-Toyo Free Talk ('Since the original story you give me is text, I constantly have your manga by my side as I draw'). So T21 DIRECTION for 1-76 is never 'the anime adapts the manga' and never 'the manga adapts the anime': eps 1-14 and 15-27 restage the two FILMS (神と神 2013 / 復活の「F」 2015) which the manga either digests in four chapters (ch 1-4) or skips entirely; eps 28-41 and 47-67 are the anime's parallel realization of the same Toriyama text the manga realizes as ch 5-13 and ch 14-26; eps 42-46 and 68-76 are Toei interludes with no source at all. STANDINGS: the stored types are right on 75 of 76 rows. ONE type correction is proposed — ep 53, whose plot (Beerus/Whis/Goku fly to Universe 10 and Goku spars with Zamasu) exists nowhere in the source; the source's counterpart beat is Kibito sparring with Zamasu while Shin visits (end of ch 16), and the manga's Beerus/Whis trip to Universe 10 is the LATER destruction visit (ch 18 = eps 58-59). Under the series' own precedent (Sean's 91/94/95: 'original episode with one restaged scene' → filler + partial) it is filler + partial{17}; AFL calls it manga canon, so it is flagged as a fork. TWO ROWS WHERE THE FANDOM FIELD LIED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS: ep 6 (party / pudding quarrel / Buu vs Beerus) really has ZERO manga pages — the manga cuts from 'Beerus and Whis arrive above Earth' (end of ch 2) straight to mid-fight (start of ch 3) — but it IS a film sequence, so it keeps canon with side_source{Battle of Gods film}, exactly the shape Sean ruled for 18-27; ep 13 carries the same 'entire events were exclusive to the anime' boilerplate and that claim is simply FALSE (ch 4 contains the Beerus Ball / Limitbreaker Kamehameha exchange ep 13 is built on, and ja-WP's 相違点 discusses that exact beat) — ep 13 stays plain canon. No `adopted` annotation anywhere in 1-76: nothing anime-original in this range (Copy-Vegeta, Ginyu's return, Pan's birth, Vegeta's apprenticeship, Super Saiyan Rage, Arale) is ever written into the manga, and the premises the manga does presuppose (Whis training, Pan) come from the RoF film, not from the anime.

annotations.note: T21 direction for the Battle of Gods arc: the anime and the manga are two INDEPENDENT realizations of the same 2013 film, not an adaptation of one another. ja-WP states it in both directions — the DBS article lists among the material Toriyama himself outlined '劇場版アニメ2作品『神と神』と『復活の「F」』を原作に用いて、各1クール分ほどのテレビシリーズアニメとして再構成・再制作した「破壊神ビルス編」と「フリーザ復活編」', and the film's own article says '『ドラゴンボール超』においては、本作を原作とした「破壊神ビルス編」として、テレビシリーズ複数話分にリメイク・再構成している'. The manga's version is a DIGEST: ja-WP '連載開始時の「破壊神ビルス編」は劇場版『神と神』のダイジェストのような内容であった', and Kanzenshuu counts the whole arc at 65 pages across four chapters (16+15+15+19) against fourteen TV episodes. Consequence for readers: every one of these rows compresses to a fraction of a chapter, and the two versions differ scene by scene — ja-WP's 相違点（破壊神ビルス編）records that in the manga Champa and Vados meet the Kaioshin and destroy Garana (absent from the anime here), that Goku's Super Saiyan God form never cancels during the fight, that Whis calls the match a draw immediately after Goku nullifies Beerus' last attack, and that Goku is never said to have absorbed the Super Saiyan God power. Fandom's per-episode 'Differences from the manga' lists a dozen more (Beerus destroys half a planet for greasy food in the anime vs the whole planet for poison in the manga; the fight is staged in the sky in the anime and in West City / the desert in the manga; ep 9's entire content is one manga page). Recorded as divergence so the block is never read as a clean transfer in either direction.

THE WORK: 『ドラゴンボールZ 神と神』 / Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods (Toei theatrical film, 2013-03-30, 85 min; 原案 = 鳥山明, 脚本 = 渡辺雄介, with ja-WP recording that over 90% of the story and dialogue came from Toriyama's own dialogue-bearing plot). Ep 6 is the ONLY row in eps 1-14 whose content has no pages at all in the identified source: the manga runs from 'Beerus and Whis then arrive above Earth' (last line of ch 2) straight into a fight already in progress at the top of ch 3, and Kanzenshuu's Beerus-arc synopsis reproduces the same jump ('the festivities have been interrupted by the arrival of two mysterious guests. After quickly dispatching Gohan, Majin Boo, and Gotenks, the uninvited guest sets his eyes on Vegeta'). Everything ep 6 is made of — Beerus and Whis being welcomed to the party by Bulma, Vegeta's placating, the octopus, the pudding quarrel and Buu vs Beerus — is in the FILM (ja-WP's あらすじ: ビルスとウイスを目の当たりにし…ベジータは…ダンスまで踊って奮闘する…そのベジータの安堵の隙にブウとビルスがプリンを巡ってケンカになってしまう). Same shape as Sean's 18-27 ruling: a second LICENSED work by the source's author, restaged — canon + side_source, no chapter mapping by design (A1). Deliberately NOT applied to the other twelve rows of the arc: they do have manga pages, and side_source there would suppress a real mapping.

T21 direction for the Universe 6 / 破壊神シャンパ編: the first arc with no film behind it, and the clearest statement of the relationship. ja-WP, verbatim: 「破壊神シャンパ編」以降は、劇場版を原作としない本作品のみのオリジナルストーリーだが、鳥山明によるストーリー原案はテキスト（文章）形式で制作スタッフに届けられる。そのストーリー原案を基にして、テレビシリーズと漫画版それぞれのスタッフが同時進行で作品を制作しているため、大筋の物語の展開は同一だが…テレビシリーズと漫画版では…どちらか一方のみにしかない場面があるなど、相互に補完する関係性となっている。' Neither direction of adaptation holds: the manga was three months ahead in publication (ch 5 2015-10-21 vs ep 28 2016-01-24) but the anime was already in production, and the anime finished the arc (ep 41, 2016-05-01) before the manga did (ch 13, 2016-06-21). Documented divergences: the scene where Whis coins 'Super Saiyan Blue' exists only in the manga (ja-WP names the pages, vol 1 pp 82-83) and the anime simply starts using the name; Goku uses Super Saiyan Blue Kaio-ken against Hit in the anime and never in the manga; the manga explains Time-Skip's limits through Whis and the anime does not; Piccolo's recruitment scene and Geppuman are anime-only; Buu fails the written exam by sleeping in the anime and by wrong answers in the manga. Every row here has source pages (fandom's chapter pages carry the reverse index ch 5→ep 28, ch 6→28-30, ch 7→31-32, ch 8→32-33, ch 9→33, ch 10→33-34, ch 11→34-37, ch 12→37-38, ch 13→39-41) — the block is canon, and the annotation records that it is a parallel telling, not a transfer.

T21 direction for the '未来'トランクス編, and the arc where the two versions diverge furthest. Same regime as the Champa arc (Toriyama's text outline realized twice, simultaneously — ja-WP: '「“未来”トランクス編」は、鳥山明が編集部の案から着想を得てストーリーを構築。そのストーリー原案を基にして、脚本家らがテレビシリーズアニメ用の脚本に仕上げている'), except that here the ANIME ran ahead in publication (ep 47 aired 2016-06-12, ch 14 published 2016-07-21; ep 67 aired 2016-11-20, ch 26 published 2017-07-18) — so the manga cannot be the anime's source, and the manga's own version was drawn while the anime was already broadcasting. Kanzenshuu's manga arc synopsis is the independent second account and it differs from the anime at almost every load-bearing beat: in the MANGA Vegeta (not Goku) dominates Goku Black with Super Saiyan God; GOKU performs the Mafuba (in the anime Future Trunks does, ep 64); Gowasu and the Kaioshin arrive early and rescue Trunks; Merged Zamasu's severed parts each REGENERATE into separate Zamasus (the anime has one 'Infinite Zamasu' spread as a mist across the universe); Future Trunks cuts Zamasu with his ordinary sword (the anime's energy 'Sword of Hope' powered by the people of Earth is anime-only); and Future Zeno erases the entire TIMELINE including its Time Ring, where the anime's erases the timeline's universes. Super Saiyan Rage (eps 61-62) is anime-exclusive by fandom's own note. In the other direction the manga adds material the anime lacks — ja-WP's 相違点（“未来”トランクス編) lists the explanation of why Trunks travels to '17 years ago', the full mechanics of the Time Rings, and why Zamasu chose Trunks' timeline (Universe 7's Kaioshin died fighting Babidi, so its God of Destruction died with him). Both versions are official; neither retcons the other.

annotations.chapters: 17 (the Gowasu-Zamasu 'are mortals worth protecting' tea conversation, relocated)
annotations.note: The single source scene inside an otherwise anime-original episode. Ep 53's cold open — Zamasu pours tea for Gowasu, asks whether mortals are worth protecting, and Gowasu answers that Kais create and observe while only the Gods of Destruction may interfere — is manga ch 17's conversation, moved: in the source it comes AFTER the Babari trip, as Gowasu's rebuke once Zamasu has killed a Babarian ('Zamasu shows confusion over the cycle of life and the purpose of humans… Gowasu tells him that that's the job of the God of Destruction while they, as Supreme Kais, are to maintain the peace… Zamasu, doubting his own role, apologizes to Gowasu and begins to prepare tea for him'). The Babari trip itself is ep 54, and ch 17's other beats (the Time Rings, the 1,000-year jump, the Grand Minister's call about Zeno) are ep 54 too. Everything else in ep 53 — Whis naming Zamasu en route, the Beerus/Whis/Goku journey, the Time Ring inspection, Goku's spar with Zamasu, the Krillin/Android 18 scene — has no counterpart. Same shape as Sean's ruling on eps 91/94/95 (an original episode carrying one restaged source scene): T28 → filler + partial. See the type_corrections entry and the flag.

type_corrections.note: Stored canon (AFL: manga canon). PROPOSED filler + partial{17}, medium confidence, flagged as a fork. The episode's own plot has zero standing in the source. (1) dragonball.fandom's ep-53 page states 'The entire events of this episode were exclusive to the anime' and then, unusually, explains the relationship: 'In the anime, Beerus, Whis and Goku travel to Universe 10 where Goku spars with Zamasu. In the manga, Shin and Kibito travel to Universe 10 where Kibito spars with Zamasu and he is told about Goku when discussing the defeat of Majin Buu and Babidi.' (2) Kanzenshuu's manga Future Trunks arc synopsis independently gives the manga's version — 'Meanwhile in Universe 10, Zamasu is training with Kibito of Universe 7 to be Gowasu's successor as Kaioshin. Learning of Majin Boo's defeat, Zamasu is astonished to hear mere mortals have achieved power surpassing that of the gods' — and places the only Beerus/Whis trip to Universe 10 much later, as the visit at which the Kaioshin's Time Ring evidence makes Beerus destroy Zamasu (manga ch 18, anime eps 58-59). (3) Corroboration in the chapter-number space: fandom's chapter pages carry a two-way index and ep 53 appears in NO chapter's episode list, while its neighbours do (ch 16 → eps 49, 51, 54; ch 17 → eps 54, 55, 57). This is a SUBSTITUTION of the same story node (Zamasu's fixation on Goku is born), which is precisely the shape Sean already ruled filler on eps 79-81 (the Zeno Expo exists in ch 28-29 as a different match entirely) and on 91/94/95 (an original episode carrying one restaged scene → filler + partial). The counter-case for keeping canon is stated in flags_for_sean.

structure.notes:
ROW IDENTITY: our 76 target rows == dragonball.fandom's List of Dragon Ball Super episodes 1-76 (131 numbered rows, no x.5 entries) == ja-WP's 各話リスト == AFL 1-76, joined on title, one for one; no shift is possible. THE SOURCE THE CATALOG SHOULD LINK: AniList manga id 86508, 『ドラゴンボール超』 (漫画 とよたろう / 原作 鳥山明, Shueisha V-Jump, first chapter 2015-06-20, 24 tankobon and 104 chapters as of 2025-04, on hiatus) — https://anilist.co/manga/86508. WHY FLAG #1016 EXISTS: AniList's relation from anime 21175 to manga 86508 is typed ALTERNATIVE, not ADAPTATION (its ADAPTATION-typed neighbours are none; the two films 14837 神と神 and 20778 復活の「F」 are also ALTERNATIVE), so pickManga is behaving correctly — the anime genuinely does not adapt the manga. A manual link is therefore needed and must be protected from any ADAPTATION-edge re-derive. CHAPTER SPACE: the V-Jump serialization's own numbering 其之一 … 其之百四 (1-104); volume boundaries for this range (ja-WP 書誌情報 + fandom volume list, agreeing): vol 1 = ch 1-9, vol 2 = ch 10-15, vol 3 = ch 16-20, vol 4 = ch 21-24, vol 5 = ch 25-28. None of these are stored (context: 0 volume boundaries). Bonus chapters (Jump Victory Carnival guidebooks, collected at the ends of vols 1, 2 and 8) are unnumbered and must stay labelled, never converted. Toyotaro's separate three-chapter 『ドラゴンボールZ 復活の「F」』 comic (V-Jump April/May/June 2015) is a DIFFERENT chapter space and must never be mixed in (batch 19 finding, unchanged).

=== SOURCE-FIELD TRAPS FOUND THIS PASS ===
(a) dragonball.fandom's chapter-page 'episode=' index is a strong two-way reverse index BUT IT DROPS ROWS: ch 3 lists eps 7-8 and omits ep 6, ch 4 lists eps 9-12, 14, 18 and omits ep 13 — in both cases the chapter's own summary settles it (ch 3 does not contain ep 6's material at all; ch 4 DOES contain ep 13's Beerus Ball / Limitbreaker Kamehameha exchange). Read it in both directions before trusting either.
(b) The per-episode 'The entire events of this episode were exclusive to the anime' boilerplate is UNRELIABLE ON BOTH SIDES in this series. It is FALSE on ep 13 (ch 4 carries the beat; ja-WP's 相違点 discusses that same exchange). It is TRUE but incomplete on ep 6 (the manga really has nothing — but the film does). Batch 19 already caught it being false across eps 20-27 against the Resurrection 'F' manga. Never take it as a standing claim alone.
(c) AFL and AFG are ONE source for types here; AFL's live Quick List reads manga canon 3, 5-14, 18-21, 23-41, 47-49, 51, 53-67; mixed 1-2; filler 4, 15, 42-46, 68-70, 73-76; anime canon 16-17, 22, 50, 52, 71-72 — i.e. AFL's 'anime canon' bucket is exactly the set Sean's T6 overrides already converted to filler.
(d) ja-WP's 各話リスト for this series carries NO filler or original marker at all (staff columns only) — it is an arc-boundary and air-date source, not a typing source.

flags_for_sean: THE STRUCTURAL FORK, AND IT IS THE BIG ONE: dragon-ball-super is not an adaptation at all. Our taxonomy defines the source as 'the work it adapts', and no work in this range fits: eps 1-27 restage two FILMS, eps 28-41 and 47-67 are Toei's realization of a prose outline that Toyotaro realizes independently as ch 5-26, and eps 42-46 and 68-76 have no parent. AniList encodes exactly this — the manga edge is typed ALTERNATIVE, not ADAPTATION, which is why flag #1016 exists and why pickManga is not broken. RECOMMENDATION: link AniList manga 86508 MANUALLY as the series' chapter space (the product promise — 'where do I pick up the manga' — is still answerable, because the manga covers the same story), and record a series-level ruling that the T21 direction is SIBLING (common outline), never adaptation, so that no future pass reads the anime as the manga's downstream or vice versa. The alternative is to leave the series manga-less, which costs every reader a position for 76 rows to buy a taxonomic nicety.

EP 53 IS THE ONE GENUINELY SPLIT ROW IN 1-76 (stored canon). FOR filler + partial{17}: fandom states outright that the entire episode is anime-exclusive and, unusually, names the manga's counterpart (Kibito spars with Zamasu, not Goku; Shin visits, not Beerus/Whis/Goku); Kanzenshuu's manga arc synopsis independently gives that same version and places the only Beerus/Whis trip to Universe 10 as the LATER destruction visit (ch 18 → eps 58-59); ep 53 appears in no chapter's episode index while both its neighbours do; and the shape — an original episode carrying one relocated source scene — is the exact shape you ruled filler + partial on 91/94/95, and the substitution logic is the one you ruled filler on 79-81. AGAINST: AFL calls it manga canon and it sits inside AFL's unbroken 53-67 canon block, and one could argue the narrative NODE (Zamasu's fixation on Goku is born in Gowasu's presence in Universe 10) is in the source and only the staging changed — which is `canon + divergence`, not filler. I have delivered the type correction at medium confidence with the partial annotation; if you prefer the block prior, drop the type correction and keep the ep-53 annotation, changing its kind from `partial` to `divergence`.

EP 6 — side_source{Battle of Gods film} on a canon row, and WHY IT IS NOT APPLIED TO THE REST OF EPS 1-14. Ep 6 is the only row in the Beerus arc with no source pages: the manga jumps from 'Beerus and Whis arrive above Earth' (end of ch 2) to a fight already in progress (start of ch 3), and Kanzenshuu's synopsis reproduces the jump; the party, Vegeta's placating dance and the pudding quarrel exist only in the FILM, whose 原案 is Toriyama (over 90% of its story and dialogue from his own dialogue-bearing plot, per ja-WP). That is the same situation as eps 18-27 and I have given it the same instrument. I deliberately did NOT annotate the other twelve non-filler rows of the arc, even though they equally restage the film, because side_source rows carry no mapping by design (A1) and those rows DO have manga pages (ch 1-4) — marking them would suppress a real, anchorable mapping. If you would rather the whole arc read consistently, the honest alternative is to record the film parentage as a series-level note rather than a per-row annotation and drop side_source from ep 6 too (it stays canon either way; only ep 4 and ep 15 are filler in the arc).

EP 13 IS A CORRECTED FALSE POSITIVE, NOT A CHANGE. Its fandom page carries the same 'entire events were exclusive to the anime' line as eps 4, 6, 15-17 and 42-46, and fandom's ch-4 episode index omits ep 13 — but ch 4's own summary contains the beat the episode is built on ('Beerus decides to use a Beerus Ball… Goku however has more power to be able to fire a Limitbreaker Kamehameha and fire back at Beerus. The Super Saiyan God form has run out'), and ja-WP's 相違点（破壊神ビルス編) discusses that exact exchange from the manga's side. Ep 13 stays plain canon. Flagged so that a future pass does not 'discover' the boilerplate and retype it.

NO `adopted` ANNOTATION ANYWHERE IN 1-76 — the honest negative, and it answers the Copy-Vegeta question in the ask. I found no case of the manga writing an anime-original EVENT into its own line within this range. Copy-Vegeta / Commeson / Planet Potaufeu never appear in the manga (fandom's Duplicate Vegeta 'MangaName=' is empty, the Copy-Vegeta Saga's 'manga chapters=' is empty, and Kanzenshuu's chapter list leaves no month for it). The premises the manga DOES take as given — Goku and Vegeta training under Whis (ch 5's opening), Pan's existence — come from the Resurrection 'F' film, not from eps 16-17, which merely dramatise how they came about; that is the reverse of adoption. Ginyu's return (ep 22), Super Saiyan Rage (eps 61-62), the Sword of Hope (ep 66) and the Arale crossovers (eps 43, 69) are all absent from the manga. Likewise NO `retconned` case: the manga's Zamasu ending does not overwrite the anime's — both are published, official and parallel, and Toriyama supervised both.

ANCHORABILITY, FOR A LATER WAVE (no numbers delivered here, per the pin). Three blocks are cleanly anchorable and one is not. Eps 28-41 and 47-67 have a complete two-way episode↔chapter index on dragonball.fandom (chapter pages' `episode=` field plus episode pages' `Manga=` field, agreeing in both directions on every row I checked) and would give a dense, honest mapping — this is the highest-value follow-up on the series. Eps 1-14 are anchor-POOR by construction: 65 manga pages against fourteen episodes, so most rows would land inside the same chapter and several would advance nothing; an END-per-row pass there risks manufacturing motion. Eps 15-27 take nothing (ruled batch 19). The stored ep-131 → ch 42 anchor (afg-continua) is consistent with the manga's Universe Survival arc ending at ch 42 (Kanzenshuu: 決着と結末, vol 9) but is outside this ask and was not re-derived.

ARC-BOUNDARY DISAGREEMENTS worth writing down once, because three sources cut this series three ways: ja-WP runs 破壊神ビルス編 = eps 1-18, フリーザ復活編 = 19-27, 破壊神シャンパ編 = 28-46, “未来”トランクス編 = 47-76, 宇宙サバイバル編 = 77-131; dragonball.fandom runs Beerus 1-15, Golden Frieza 16-27, Universe 6 28-41, Copy-Vegeta 42-46, Future Trunks 47-74 (+ an anime-only 'Paradise Plant Saga' for 75-76); Kanzenshuu's episode guide uses Battle of Gods / Resurrection 'F' / Champa / Future Trunks / Universe Survival. None of it moves a standing — every row's type here was decided on content, not on which arc header sits above it — but the ask's five-arc split (1-14 / 15-27 / 28-41 / 42-46 / 47-76) matches no single source exactly and should be treated as our own convention.
